open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin” does not define the cookie's Domain, Path, SameSite or Secure behaviour, and HTTP cookies cannot be restricted by port as an origin can
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “only to Registry's own origin,” including access on the Registry host without HTTPS?
options: A host-only, HttpOnly cookie with Path=/ and an explicit SameSite policy
A dedicated Registry hostname with a __Host- cookie that is always Secure
Some other server-enforced origin binding in addition to the cookie
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only __Host- session cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/ and SameSite=Strict, requiring HTTPS for every browser connection.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession pending import confirmation
open_points.text: The changed disclosure table classifies “the owner session, but for its uploaded import file” as business_confidential, while changed M11 keeps “the inputs it is bound to” and A13 binds an import confirmation to “the picks, names, aliases and Customer values”; names and Customer values are personal_data
open_points.question: Does the pending confirmation store those personal values, or only a non-reversible binding to values resubmitted with the confirmation?
options: Store the full mapping inputs and classify those OwnerSession facts as personal_data
Store only digests or another non-reversible binding and require the values to be resubmitted
Keep the mapping in a separate personal_data session object
open_points.default_guess: Store only a canonical digest of the mapping inputs and apply values resubmitted with the confirmed request after verifying the digest.

open_points.subject: A15 empty audit erasure
open_points.text: R0-66 says an audit erasure “leaves an entry of its own naming the date,” but A15 rule 6 says an erasure that removes no entry “writes no entry and mints no confirmation id”
open_points.question: Must an accepted erasure that finds no qualifying entry append an erasure entry?
options: Always append an erasure entry
Append one only when at least one old entry was removed
open_points.default_guess: Append one only when at least one entry was removed, following A14's changed-state rule.

open_points.subject: A16 validation scope of the mapping
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows “every malformed record and every id that conflicts with one production holds,” while rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects “are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported”
open_points.question: Are malformed records and production conflicts reported for the whole file or only for the picked projects and records they bring in?
options: Validate and report the whole file
Validate and report only picked project subgraphs, except the file-level checks explicitly made at upload
Parse the whole file but report only faults that affect a pick
open_points.default_guess: Apply only the two stated file-level upload checks globally and validate all other malformations and conflicts only within picked project subgraphs.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup
open_points.text: “Right after an accepted import Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule, so the import reaches a checked backup as soon as it can; a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays accepted” does not say whether the import response waits for that run, how a pending failed import backup is remembered, or which later run retries it
open_points.question: When does the import-triggered backup run relative to the import response, and how is its retry obligation scheduled and persisted?
options: Run and check it synchronously before answering, without making backup success part of import success
Answer after commit and run it asynchronously, persisting a pending-backup marker
Answer after commit and make only one best-effort attempt, relying on the next ordinary daily run
open_points.default_guess: Commit and answer the import, then run the backup asynchronously and persist a pending-import-backup marker until a checked backup containing the closure exists.

open_points.subject: Uploaded import file lifetime
open_points.text: The changed texts make the uploaded import file personal_data and say it is “kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in the store” and dropped on replacement, acceptance or session end, but do not say whether it is held in memory or on disk, who can read it, or how crash and restart remnants are removed
open_points.question: Where may the uploaded personal-data file be stored, and what cleanup and access-isolation rules apply on normal expiry, replacement, crash and restart?
options: Memory only, bounded by the State 6 size limit
A protected encrypted temporary file with startup cleanup
Either representation under an explicit private runtime-storage contract
open_points.default_guess: Keep it in memory only and discard it with the non-durable OwnerSession state.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only configuration test
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits an owner-only start with “none of the four” service tokens, but required test 1 says “A configuration without Client Portal's token stops the start” without limiting that test to a partial token set
open_points.question: Does a configuration with no Client Portal token start successfully when all four service tokens are absent?
options: Yes; only an all-or-none token set is valid
No; Client Portal's token is always mandatory, so owner-only start is not valid
open_points.default_guess: Yes; zero service tokens is the owner-only mode, while any nonempty incomplete set fails.

open_points.subject: A17 store and backup location separation
open_points.text: “The store and the backup location are different places, neither inside the other” does not define how equality and containment are determined in the presence of relative paths, symbolic links, hard links, bind mounts or path changes after startup
open_points.question: What filesystem identity and containment check must Registry use to accept or refuse the configured locations?
options: Compare normalized path strings only
Resolve existing paths and compare canonical filesystem locations
Treat mount and link safety entirely as host administration and check only lexical containment
open_points.default_guess: Resolve both locations to canonical existing parent paths, reject equal or ancestor relationships after resolution, and fail startup if they cannot be resolved safely.

open_points.subject: A18 import backup versus daily quota
open_points.text: Rule 1 says “Besides the run after an accepted import, at most one backup is kept per UTC day,” but also says a missed run is made at startup only “if no backup was made that UTC day”
open_points.question: Does an import-triggered backup count as the day's backup and suppress the ordinary 03:00 or startup run, or may both an import backup and one ordinary daily backup be kept that day?
options: The import backup counts as that day's backup
The import backup is additional, and one ordinary daily backup may also be kept
Whether it counts depends on whether it ran before or after 03:00 UTC
open_points.default_guess: Treat the import backup as additional and allow one separate ordinary daily backup for the UTC day.

open_points.subject: A18 startup catch-up run
open_points.text: A missed 03:00 run “is made when it next starts with its service tokens,” while A17 says Registry serves after configuration checks; the texts do not say whether service traffic is admitted before the catch-up backup and its check finish
open_points.question: Must a service-enabled startup complete the due backup run before serving requests, or may it begin serving while the run proceeds?
options: Complete the run before serving
Begin serving and run the backup concurrently
Begin serving, then run the backup serially in the background
open_points.default_guess: Begin serving after startup checks and perform the catch-up backup as a non-overlapping background run.

open_points.subject: A18 replay of audit-log erasures after restore
open_points.text: Rule 10 requires the owner to “erase audit entries before the latest date the owner erased by,” but “latest date” may mean the date supplied by the most recent erasure action or the greatest cutoff date ever applied
open_points.question: Which cutoff must be replayed when audit-erasure actions were performed with non-monotonic dates?
options: The greatest cutoff date ever applied
The cutoff supplied by the chronologically most recent erasure action
Every recorded erasure action in its original order
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest cutoff date ever applied, since earlier entries must not be revived by a restore.

open_points.subject: A18 retention-deletion failure
open_points.text: Registry “deletes every backup” older than 30 days, but “a deletion that fails” is merely reported and retried at the next run; the rules do not say whether deletion continues for the remaining expired backups or whether the run stops at the first failure
open_points.question: After one expired backup cannot be deleted, must Registry continue attempting the other expired backups and the rest of the run?
options: Continue independently with every expired backup
Stop all retention deletion at the first failure
Make deletion of the expired set atomic
open_points.default_guess: Continue attempting every expired backup independently and report each failure.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id lifetime after erasure
open_points.text: Rule 1 requires a request id to be “unique for every create it means as new” and R0-36 says a repeated create “never silently makes a second” record, but rule 8 says erasure or anonymisation removes the stored request id and “a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create”
open_points.question: Is the same request id permanently tied to its original create, or may it create a second record after the original idempotency fact is erased?
options: Retain a non-personal request-id tombstone so the repeat never creates again
Allow reuse after erasure or anonymisation as rule 8 states
Refuse the request without recreating while the surviving erased identity exists, but allow it after whole deletion
open_points.default_guess: Retain a minimal request-id tombstone and never treat the same request id as a new create.

open_points.subject: A04 failures within one check stage
open_points.text: Rule 6 says “the first failure is its answer” and orders owner checks as “a valid owner session, then its CSRF value, then a confirmation value,” but then says “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them”
open_points.question: Within a stage, does Registry stop at the first ordered failure or aggregate all failures, including checks that cannot safely or meaningfully run after an earlier failure?
options: Stop at the first failing check within each stage
Aggregate every independently evaluable failure in the stage
Return one generic stage failure while recording no individual failures
open_points.default_guess: Stop at the first ordered failure within a stage, especially for authentication and authorization checks.
